title: Transaction history not showing new transfers after sync (v1.5.2 and v1.5.3)
body:
Description:

First, I want to say this is the best Zcash client I've ever used — thank you for the great work.

I'm running into a bug with transaction history. Here's what happened:

Background:
Recently I was unable to sync blocks or send Zcash at all.

After updating to v1.5.2:
Block syncing and sending transactions started working again. However, new transfer records do not appear in the transaction history, even though the transactions go through successfully.

After updating to v1.5.3 (latest):
The issue is still not resolved — new transfers are still missing from the transaction history.

Steps to Reproduce:

Update to v1.5.2 or v1.5.3
Let the wallet sync blocks
Send a Zcash transaction (it completes successfully)
Open the transaction history
Expected Behavior:
The new transfer should appear in the transaction history.

Actual Behavior:
The transaction completes, but it does not show up in the transaction history list.

title: Issues with sending fund - failed to validate tx:.......
body:
Hello,

I'm having an issue with YWallet on Windows (v1.14.0+564).

My main wallet shows the correct balance and transaction history, but any attempt to send funds fails with:

failed to validate tx: WtxId("private"), error:
transaction did not pass consensus validation:
transaction uses an incorrect consensus branch id

I have tried multiple servers (Zec.rocks and Zcash Infra) with the same result.

I also tried restoring the wallet using my saved seed and keys. The restored wallet generates a different Unified Viewing Key and a different Unified Address than the original Main wallet, and shows a zero balance.

The original Main wallet still shows the correct balance and transaction history.

Is this a known issue, or is there a recommended way to recover the original account and restore spending functionality?

I can provide screenshots, TXID, addresses, viewing keys, and backup information if needed.

Thank you.

title: Crash on Startup (SIGABRT) during "Load Active Account" (get_txs)
body:
# Bug Report: Crash on Startup During Active Account Load 

## Description
YWallet crashes immediately upon startup on Android. The logs indicate that the app initializes the databases correctly but fails during the final stages of loading the active account. Specifically, the crash occurs during a native call to `get_txs`.

## Device Information
* **Device:** Motorola Moto G7 (Codename: 'river')
* **OS:** Android 10 (Build QPUS30.52-16-2-13)
* **App Version:** 1.14.1 (Installed via Google Play)

## Logcat Analysis
The crash occurs after the database migration and ZEC/YEC initialization. A fatal signal 6 (`SIGABRT`) is triggered in the native layer:

```log
03-26 17:41:31.339 10436 10582 I flutter : 0.8 Load Active Account
03-26 17:41:31.379 10436 10582 F libc    : Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT), code -1 (SI_QUEUE) in tid 10582 (2.ui), pid 10436 (me.hanh.ywallet)
```


Backtrace Highlights: The crash appears to originate from the Rust/FFI layer within the get_txs function:

## Code snippet
#10 pc 00000000006668ec ... split_config.arm64_v8a.apk (get_txs+6940)
Additional Context:
There is also a PlatformException related to SHARED_PREFERENCES_NOT_AVAILABLE from the awesome_notifications package occurring just before the native crash:

## Code snippet
Unhandled Exception: PlatformException(SHARED_PREFERENCES_NOT_AVAILABLE, class f5.b isn't parameterized, sharedPreferences.get, null)
Steps to Reproduce
Open YWallet.

The splash screen appears and the app logs "Load Active Account."

The app abruptly crashes to the home screen (or displays an "App has stopped" dialog).

## Proposed Solution / User Impact
Currently, this native crash prevents access to the UI and the backup menu, completely locking out users who have not yet backed up their seed phrase.

To allow users to recover their wallets in this state, please consider updating the Rust implementation to gracefully handle the underlying cause of the get_txs panic. Passing an error state back up to the Flutter UI—instead of allowing the process to abort entirely—would keep the application alive long enough for users to access the settings and securely back up their seed phrase.


I am software developer, if you guide me I can help with this.

title: enhancement: better UX re: connectivity
body:
Currently the app does not display enough info for the user to fully understand the connection state to Zcash servers. This could lead to changing settings unnecessarily, etc.

## Issue 1:

App may say "DISCONNECTED." Tapping the word "DISCONNECTED" does nothing. No indication is given whether the app is trying to connect, has given up connecting, etc.

### Desired enhancement(s):

* App should indicate whether it is trying to connect or not
* If connection has failed, app should indicate why (timeout, DNS, network error)

## Issue 2:

App may display a numeric block height (or a catch up % if user taps) and appear to make no progress for a long time without indicating what is happening.

### Desired enhancement(s):

* App should indicate if data is being transferred or not so the user can have insight into whether the sync is actually proceeding
   * Alternately, the sync status should be updated on the display more frequently
* If the server disconnects or there is a network error, it should be displayed
   * Alternately, revert to a "DISCONNECTED" state with enhancements as discussed above
* Consider implementing automatic failover to a second-choice server

Thank you for your work on Ywallet.

title: Android: temporary freeze when switching Zcash servers
body:
When I switch Zcash servers in the Android app (on Android 12, currently) there is a freeze of one minute or longer where the UI becomes completely unresponsive.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Be syncing a wallet that's behind (not sure if this is necessary to reproduce but this is where I'm seeing it)
2. Observe that the sync is not making progress
3. Open settings
4. Tap a different Zcash Infrastructure server
5. Tap the checkmark in the upper right

## Actual result

The UI completely freezes for at least a minute or longer.

## Expected result

The UI remains responsive, with a throbber displayed if switching servers needs to block for a while.
